_comment: Which reviewers are REQUIRED for the files the branch changes (committed since the base branch plus staged). 'always' run on every substantive commit. Patterns use fnmatch (a single * also matches across /). Tuned for stock-explorer-app: dbt project in dbt_analytics/, Python ingestion in ingestion/, Streamlit app in frontend/, Supabase export/migrations in supabase/. A commit is exempt (bookkeeping) when the branch's whole cumulative diff matches artifact_only, except anything in artifact_only_never.
_comment_guard_paths: GUARD PATHS (modeled on football-data-pipeline's routing). .claude/settings.json auto-launches hook commands every session, the same authority class as a CI workflow file -- routed to platform-reviewer. .claude/working-agreement.md governs every agent action in this repo (protocol, branch rules, decision rights) and is routed to platform-reviewer for the same reason. .gitlab-ci.yml routed to platform-reviewer for CI authority (.github/workflows/* is a dead pattern from before the GitLab migration). .claude/hooks/* and .claude/agents/* are routed to platform-reviewer: every hook and every reviewer role lives in this repo, so an edit to a gate or a reviewer appears in the staged diff and is reviewed like code. This file routing to itself means any FUTURE edit to it requires platform-reviewer -- it does NOT stop a single commit from weakening a rule and exploiting the weakened rule in the same breath: commit_review_gate.py reads this file from its current staged/working-tree state with no baseline pinning. Protection against that needs football-data-pipeline's protected_override mechanism, a code change to commit_review_gate.py, deliberately not built here.
